subject: English
passage: A study by Dr. Channary Sok and colleagues concluded that people are more likely to remember new information accurately when they take handwritten notes rather than type notes on a computer. Study participants were assigned to one of two groups. The experimental group took notes by hand while watching an educational video, and the control group typed notes on laptops while watching the same video. One week later, both groups took a quiz on the video content. Sok and colleagues found that the experimental group scored significantly higher on the quiz than the control group did.
prompt: Which choice best describes the main purpose of the text?

choices.A: To describe a commonly accepted theory and how a study's results validate that theory
choices.B: To argue that researchers were disappointed by the outcome of a particular study
choices.C: To explain a study's conclusion and how a research team arrived at that conclusion
choices.D: To recommend modifications to a particular study's research methodology

explanation: Choice C is the best answer because the text explains a study's conclusion and how the research team arrived at it. The passage begins by summarizing the main conclusion: people remember information more accurately when taking handwritten notes rather than typing. It then describes the experimental design—participants either took notes by hand (experimental group) or typed on laptops (control group) while watching an educational video. By comparing quiz performance one week later, Sok and colleagues found the experimental group scored significantly higher, which led to the conclusion stated at the beginning.
